findings.issue: Bits Dialog.Content default FocusScope captures focus across the owner document, beyond the owned application.
findings.evidence: Installed Bits FocusScope mechanism in transparent Node/HappyDOM harness: requested Application B, actual Drawer A, focusStolen:true. No rendered-browser claim; initial untransformed $state error retained.
findings.boundary: trapFocus=false removes recapture and Tab loop but still registers global FocusScopeManager; independent manager arbitration remains.

findings.issue: Explicit panelStyle replaces presentation.target(panel).style and drops runtime --ui-binding variables.
findings.evidence: Canonical panel opacity binding compiles; Svelte compiler confirms explicit style getter replaces spread style. Static backdrop-only checks did not cover it.

findings.issue: Default TextSelectionLayer changes ownerDocument.body.userSelect; EscapeLayer consumes document Escape and shares global arbitration.
findings.evidence: Installed Bits UI2.19.3 source: EscapeLayer calls original event.preventDefault before checking ignore/defer behavior. No public Dialog.Content option disables EscapeLayer or FocusScope registration entirely.
findings.qualification: preventOverflowTextSelection=false genuinely disables selection layer. preventScroll=false disables global scroll lock. Neither resolves Escape/focus ownership.
